message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative measure of agreement between animal model (mouse) and human results ('the majority of real P-sites in the mouse could be inferred from the experimentally derived human P-sites with PTMoreR mapping'). It also compares phosphoproteomes across 129 mammalian species, including quantitative comparisons of P-site conservation and differential expression.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "The study develops and validates a tool (PTMoreR) for cross-species PTM mapping, focusing on the methodology and its application to assess concordance and differences in PTMs across species.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) and their conservation across mammalian species, which is a fundamental biological process relevant to many therapeutic areas rather than a specific disease.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes and compares phosphoproteomes across 129 mammalian species, including human and mouse, and also uses data from other species like monkeys, dogs, cats, etc.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "non-human-primate",
    "dog",
    "cat",
    "pig",
    "rabbit",
    "sheep",
    "horse",
    "cattle"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly mentions and analyzes data from human, mouse, rat, monkey (green monkey Vero E6 cells), cow, dog, horse, cat, rabbit, sheep, and pig.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study focuses on mapping and comparing protein post-translational modifications (PTMs), specifically phosphorylation sites, and their associated motifs and kinase-substrate networks, which are considered biomarkers."
}
